title: Pillars of Creation, Hubble 1995 and 2014
headline: Hubble 1995 and 2014
caveats: Aligned on 15 stars to about 0.1 arcsecond on average. The 1995 picture is a mosaic of four detectors that do not line up perfectly with each other, so in places the two images can be offset by up to 0.3 arcsecond, about 3 pixels of the 1995 image. A shift that small is an alignment limit, not motion in the nebula.
alignment: Alignment: about 0.1 arcsecond, up to 0.3 in places.

registration.method: similarity, least squares on 15 star control points (science review, 2026-11-17)
registration.notes: One similarity for the whole mosaic, by decision; the fit is not per chip. The WFPC2 release mosaic keeps per-chip offsets: with a shared scale, chip translations relative to WF-BR are WF-TL (-2.8, -6.9), WF-BL (-2.6, -1.2) and PC (-1.6, -2.5) 2014 px, up to about 7.5 2014 px (0.3 arcsec) between WF-TL and WF-BR; a translation per chip would bring the RMS from 2.56 to 1.66 px (90 inliers). Held out of the fit: S16 (WF-TL) 1995 (486.44, 195.24) to 2014 (3057.02, 922.66); S17 (WF-BL) 1995 (264.62, 1179.22) to 2014 (2203.6, 3276.26); S18 (WF-BR) 1995 (1193.62, 1330.51) to 2014 (4439.43, 3940.82); residuals 2.02, 2.59 and 0.50 px (2014). Details: docs/science/pillars.md, part 2.

whatDiffers: Same telescope, two cameras: WFPC2 in 1995 and WFC3 in 2014, about 19 years apart. Both map oxygen to blue, hydrogen to green and sulfur to red, but through different filters: the 2014 green filter is wider and also lets in nitrogen light. Each image was processed separately, so differences in color, brightness and how stars look come from the cameras and processing, not from the nebula. The 2014 image is sharper and covers a wider field.

validation.notes: Accepted with caveats by science review: band and processing differ, note replaced, alignment caveat added, no claim about the fragment or the jet. docs/science/pillars.md, Validation.
